title: Horizon Annotator: Route & Model Performance Explorer with Cost Scenarios
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Design and prototype a compact explorer focused on per-route and per-model performance with an integrated cost-scenario panel. The 'Horizon Annotator' is intended as a lightweight overlay that product teams can use to: (1) compare latency/throughput/token metrics across model variants and routes, (2) toggle cost scenarios (batching, quantization, routing policy) to preview unit economics, and (3) annotate anomalies or rollout notes inline for SRE/PM handoff. This work covers high-fidelity mockups, chart interaction specs, accessibility considerations, and an engineering handoff packet for SDK/telemetry requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive explorer renders per-route and per-model lanes and supports zero-to-60ms and 95th percentile overlays
Cost scenario toggles apply instantly to estimates and display delta overlays (absolute and percent)
Waterfall quantile selector updates the latency waterfall and microtrace sparkline in-context
Annotations persist on the route and are visible in the rollouts timeline and in export CSV
Design tokens, color palette, and contrast meet WCAG AA for all chart elements
chart_spec_summary: 1) Lane view: stacked small-multiples for routes grouped by model variant; y-axis auto-normalize per-lane with optional fixed-scale toggle. 2) Latency waterfall: stacked quantiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) rendered as bands with median line and hover microtrace peek. 3) Throughput sparkline: per-second TPS with configurable smoothing window. 4) Token ribbon: stacked bars showing prompt vs. completion tokens and per-token cost overlay. 5) Cost scenario overlay: translucent projected-cost bands for different batching and quantization profiles. Data granularity: 1s for microtraces, 1m aggregated for overview tiles. Recommended color tokens: blue-600 median, purple-500 p95, orange-500 cost-delta, gray-300 background band.
interactions: Hover lane -> show quick stats (latency p50/p95, TPS, tokens, cost per 1k tokens)
Click quantile band -> open mini microtrace popover with top 3 correlated traces
Toggle cost scenario -> animate overlay transition and recalc delta badge
Drag select time range -> update all charts and enable export/annotate actions
Pin route -> add to 'investigate' list in Rollouts timeline
tradeoffs: Compact small-multiples improve scan speed but reduce absolute-y comparability; added fixed-scale toggle mitigates this
Rendering microtrace peeks on hover increases client CPU; limit to sampled traces and server-side prefetching
Displaying cost projections client-side avoids extra API calls but requires shipping quantization profiles embedded in config
review_comments: PM (Anika Rao): 'Love the cost scenario slider — can we include a 'savings threshold' alert when >20%?'
Eng (Rafael Gomez): 'Need clear telemetry contract for microtrace peek to avoid expanding DB queries; prefer batched fetch endpoints.'
Design (Noor Sethi): 'Consider a compact legend overlay to reduce visual noise at narrow widths.'
SRE (Jordan Lee): 'Annotations must be immutable once signed off by on-call; consider versioning.'

accessibility_notes: All interactive controls are keyboard-focusable, charts expose data via aria-describedby summary. Color-only encodings have patterns for p99 and cost overlays. Provide CSV export for screen-reader consumption.
notes_for_engineering: API must provide: per-route time-series for latency quantiles, per-trace microtrace samples (bounded & sampled), token counts split by prompt/completion, and cost-projection endpoint that accepts batching and quantization parameters. Prefer aggregated 1m endpoints with a separate microtrace sample API. Use server-side caching for cost projections and include ETag for delta updates.
